 TheIndustry.beauty Awards Winners’ Interview: Ultra Violette founder Ava Chandler-Matthews on transforming suncare through skincare-led innovation 
 Sophie Smith 21 October 2026 
 Twitter 
 Facebook 
 Linkedin 
 WhatsApp 
 TheIndustry.beauty Innovators Awards 2026 celebrated the people, products and businesses driving the beauty industry forward, recognising not only groundbreaking innovations but also the diverse range of expertise, disciplines and leadership required to achieve true market distinction. 
 Australian suncare brand Ultra Violette took home the award for Best New Product: SPF (Prestige or Luxe) for Future Fluid, its ultra-lightweight mineral SPF 50+ serum. Designed to deliver high-level sun protection with a natural, skin-perfected finish, the formula helps shield skin from harmful UV rays and the visible signs of premature ageing.
 Future Fluid is part of Ultra Violette’s wider range of SPF skincare products. Pioneering the sunscreen-meets-skincare category, the brand has redefined daily sun protection with its SKINSCREENS - products that combine high-performance UVA and UVB protection with skincare benefits. With a focus on helping protect against sun damage, including wrinkles, fine lines and pigmentation, Ultra Violette champions the importance of daily SPF as one of the most effective ways to support long-term skin health.
 In this interview, founder Ava Chandler-Matthews shares her approach to identifying untapped opportunities in the market and translating consumer insights into innovative, much-loved products. She also discusses the thinking behind award-winning Future Fluid, the biggest opportunities and challenges shaping the beauty industry today, and her ambitions for the future of Ultra Violette.
 And in our exclusive video from this year’s awards ceremony, Amber Maloney, General Manager for the UK and Europe, shares her reaction to the win.
 What are the core values that define Ultra Violette and how are they brought to life across the business? 
 Ultra Violette was born from the concept of taking the grunt work out of SPF. Sunscreen is the most important step in any skincare routine, the one thing your dermatologist will tell you to do every day, but in the past, formulations were typically thick, oily and greasy and didn’t slot easily into an everyday beauty regimen. Our number one aim is for more people to apply sunscreen every day, and that’s what motivates everything we do – from the formulation, texture, packaging and tone of voice. Nothing makes us happier than hearing someone say that they now wear SPF daily because of one of our products.
 What’s your approach to identifying gaps in the market and how do you transform those insights into successful, consumer-loved products? 
 [Co-founder] Bec [Jefferd] and I met working in product development at a major Australian beauty retailer, and we realised that there was nothing sexy about sunscreens, from the way they looked, felt and smelt to how they were marketed and where they were sold. It felt like an afterthought for a lot of skincare brands, rather than the VIP that it should be. Because of our beauty background, we approached the formulation of our range from a skincare starting point and created a wardrobe of SPF that targeted as many pain points as possible – anything from a radiant to a matte finish, and products that work for various skin sensitivities.
 We’re constantly asking: what other need – product, texture, ingredient – can we address to make daily SPF application easier and more enjoyable for more people? Our community plays a huge role in this. Talking directly with our customers helps us with future product development, what needs to be tweaked and what’s working or not.
 Ultra Violette won at TheIndustry.beauty Awards. In your view, what set this product apart and resonated most with both the judges and wider consumers? 
 Typically, mineral formulas are thick, hard to blend and often leave a white cast. Future Fluid is super lightweight and leaves a glowy, skin-perfected finish. We really wanted to turn the perception of zinc on its head: it can be lightweight and cosmetically elegant. When feeling the texture of Future, people are astounded at how light it is. The dry-down and finish are almost imperceptible. We predicted we might convert some mineral sunscreen haters with this formula, and it has become one of our most popular products globally. Personally, I don’t like a lot of mineral sunscreens, but I love this product, and many of our team are now converts too!
 Can you share some further insights into the development process? What were the key priorities you focused on to ensure the product delivered in terms of performance and overall user experience? 
 With Future, we wanted to create something more wearable, blendable and hydrating, with a glowier finish. We used an innovative, lightweight zinc from Japan that sinks into the skin more seamlessly, along with iron oxides to help minimise white cast (which is typical for zinc formulas due to zinc being a white powder). It’s formulated as an oil-in-water emulsion rather than water-in-oil, which is what gives it that incredibly light feel.
 Zinc is an anti-inflammatory, but that also means it can be drying at times, so we added super hydrators like Pentavitin and squalane to make sure it works across many different skin types. We also conducted testing on various skin tones. We take our product development very seriously, so all of our products go through various rounds of rigorous testing until we get them just right.
 What did winning Best New Product SPF (Prestige & Luxe) represent for Ultra Violette and how does this recognition reflect the brand’s achievements, vision and contribution to the industry? 
 This recognition is such a proud moment for the whole team. From the outset, we wanted to pioneer the transformation of suncare into a skincare staple on a global scale, proving the Australian proposition of daily application translates to other markets and consumers.
 We have a dedicated product development team who work very hard to identify gaps we can fill in our range. We know it really comes down to the product you want to wear every day, so we always focus on perfecting our textures and finishes. Because of our climate, Australia is quite sophisticated and progressive when it comes to sunscreen development and the range of SPF filters we have available to us. Recognition like this is proof of how well our formulations stack up against global SPF brands.
 What do you believe are the biggest opportunities and challenges shaping the beauty sector today and how is Ultra Violette positioned to navigate this evolving landscape? 
 To speak to the sun category specifically, SPF formulations have come a LONG way in the past 10 years. Sunscreen has really emerged as its own beauty category, and the competition is steep, with a huge number of brands emerging in the space, particularly with the K-beauty craze. Consumers are more educated, and they now expect much more: no white cast, a lightweight, wearable texture and additional skincare benefits. People are no longer willing to put up with breakouts, eyes that sting, white cast and thick creams. If the aim is daily application, the products need to feel like best-in-class skincare.
 Another big challenge is the worrying amount of misinformation on social media – the ‘sunscreen is toxic’ narrative, the tan lines trend, beef tallow as natural sun protection! Emphatic misinformation like this tends to go viral and can so easily influence large groups of people in negative ways. We’ll continue our mission to educate and develop beautiful formulas in the hope that more people adopt this very important daily habit.
 How does innovation drive Ultra Violette’s growth strategy and how does the brand identify, develop and respond to emerging consumer needs and market opportunities? 
 Continuing to innovate in product is something that keeps us awake at night, but we love the process and wouldn’t change anything! Our product development team is constantly trying out new formulations, textures and finishes to cater for all skin types so that there is really something for everyone in our range. We like to say we have a wardrobe of products, so you might have a variety of SPF products in your beauty arsenal depending on the occasion (girls' lunch, workout, post-skin treatment) or even just whatever kind of finish you feel like on your skin that day.
 As you become more global as a brand, you need to think about customers in other parts of the world. What is going to work in the Canadian snow won’t work for drier, hot climates like Los Angeles, so that’s another layer of complexity we need to consider in product development.
 As the beauty industry continues to evolve, what does the future look like for Ultra Violette, and what ambitions and priorities will shape the brand’s next chapter of growth? 
 We are always working away on new and exciting products to innovate in the SPF space - we have products lined up until 2028! Our US business is accelerating, so we are exploring new ways to increase our brand awareness in this market in particular.
 Ultimately, our ambition remains the same: to make SPF application easier than ever and a joy to wear, so that more people wear sunscreen every single day. We really hope everyone can find their perfect SPF match in our range.
